title: Quasi-coherent cohomology over an affine base is higher-image sections
statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative ring, let $T=\operatorname{Spec}A$ be its affine scheme [def-pc-scheme], and let $p:Z\to T$ be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated morphism of algebraic spaces [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Quasi-compact means that inverse images of quasi-compact spaces are quasi-compact; quasi-separated means that the diagonal is quasi-compact. For every quasi-coherent module $M$ on the small etale ringed site of $Z$ [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module] and every integer $q\geq0$ there is a canonical natural isomorphism
$$ H^q(Z,M)\;\cong\;\Gamma(T,R^qp_*M). $$
Here $H^q$ is the right derived functor of global sections of module sheaves on the small etale site, and $R^qp_*$ is the right derived functor of module direct image [def-trf-space-etale-module-functors], both computed by injective resolutions in all module sheaves. There is no Noetherian assumption on $A$ and no finite-type or coherence assumption on $M$.

source.place: Tag 08EX, lemma-quasi-coherence-higher-direct-images-application, with the affine object V=T.

proof.text: For each $b\geq0$, apply [lem-sfb-space-higher-direct-image-quasi-coherent] to the given qcqs morphism $p$ and quasi-coherent module $M$. Thus $N_b=R^bp_*M$ is quasi-coherent on $T_{\mathrm{et}}$. Both required morphism hypotheses occur in the item; no properness or finite presentation is used.

For any quasi-coherent module $N$ on $T_{\mathrm{et}}$, [lem-trf-scheme-zariski-etale-quasi-coherent-equivalence] gives a quasi-coherent Zariski module $G$ and $N\cong G_{\mathrm{et}}$. By [lem-sc-etale-affine-qcoherent], its underlying abelian sheaf has zero positive cohomology on affine $T$. To check the module convention, apply [lem-sfb-module-resolution-derived-presheaf-comparison] to a module resolution $N\to I^\bullet$ and an abelian resolution $UN\to J^\bullet$. Its comparison $\iota UI^\bullet\to\iota J^\bullet$ is a quasi-isomorphism of presheaf complexes. Evaluating at the terminal etale object $T$ preserves kernels and cokernels, since these are objectwise in presheaves. Consequently the two section complexes have the same cohomology. The former computes module cohomology and the latter abelian cohomology. Hence $H^a(T,N)=0$ for $a>0$ in the module convention too. Taking $N=N_b$ gives $H^a(T,R^bp_*M)=0$ for all $a>0,b\geq0$.

By [lem-trf-space-enlarged-etale-ringed-site-model], $p$ induces the canonical morphism of ringed small etale topoi $(\mathrm{Sh}(Z_{\mathrm{et}}),\mathcal O_Z)\to(\mathrm{Sh}(T_{\mathrm{et}}),\mathcal O_T)$: it is realized by the continuous fibre-product functor $v_p:\mathcal C_T\to\mathcal C_Z$ of the enlarged ringed sites, transported through the scheme-restriction equivalences of topoi and of module categories. These equivalences preserve injectives and global sections, so module cohomology may be computed on either model. By [lem-trf-space-chart-limit-enlarged-sections], the module direct image $Q_p$ of this morphism has a natural isomorphism $\alpha_p:p_*\xrightarrow{\sim}Q_p$ from the direct image fixed by [def-trf-space-etale-module-functors], compatible with every chart projection. Hence $R^bp_*M\cong R^bQ_pM$, computed from one injective resolution of $M$, compatibly with the images of cocycles. Apply [lem-sfb-ringed-site-leray-spectral-sequence] to this morphism of ringed topoi and to $M$ in degree zero. This gives a natural first-quadrant spectral sequence $E_2^{a,b}=H^a(T,R^bp_*M)$ abutting to $H^{a+b}(Z,M)$, with the stated finite filtration and cocycle edge map.

Only column $a=0$ survives on the second page. For $r\geq2$, an incoming differential to $(0,q)$ starts in negative first degree, and an outgoing one lands in the zero column $a=r>0$. Thus $E_\infty^{0,q}=E_2^{0,q}$ and every other graded piece of total degree $q$ is zero. Starting from $\mathrm{Fil}^{q+1}=0$ gives $\mathrm{Fil}^1=0$, so the edge is an isomorphism $H^q(Z,M)\cong E_2^{0,q}=\Gamma(T,R^qp_*M)$. Its naturality and independence of resolution are those of the edge in step 3. At $q=0$ this is the ordinary equality of global sections; zero modules and empty schemes give zero groups throughout.
